title: Listing intake: sidecar partner checklist + snippet lab
content:
Purpose:
This is a focused intake playbook for partners shipping Redwood as a "sidecar" (embedded inference / connector) into their SaaS or cloud product and listing that integration in cloud marketplaces. The doc is meant to be used by BizDev, Partner Ops, Product Partnerships, and the small cross-functional launch teams doing preflight copy + tech gating.

Scope / definition:
- "Sidecar" = partner bundle or connector where Redwood runs inference adjacent to partner workloads (hosted or VPC) and is surfaced via partner UI or API. This doc covers listing copy variants, acceptance criteria, lightweight tech checks, telemetry hooks, and launch contingencies for marketplace tiles and publisher listings. Not for full private-deploy contracts (see Private deployment playbook).

Quick intake flow (one-page):
1) Partner onboarding form -> PM reviews (BizDev).
2) Early tile copy draft (this doc) -> iterate with partner comms.
3) Lightweight technical preflight -> infra engineer sign-off.
4) Legal & billing review for SKU mapping.
5) QA and telemetry smoke tests.
6) Publish to marketplace (soft-launch) + validate telemetry for 72h.
7) Post-launch readout and small-batch marketing.

Role owners (default):
- BizDev / Partner Owner: Aisha Patel (owner for intake)
- Launch PM: Marco Diaz
- Engineering preflight: Sophie Nguyen
- Billing / Marketplace ops: Ishaan Rao
- Legal touchpoint: LegalMarketplace@redwood.com

Cue cards: tile copy primitives (short obligations)
- 8–12 word tagline (max): "Add fast, production-grade LLM inference to your app."
- 1-line elevator (30–50 chars): "Real-time LLM features with predictable costs."
- 2-line blurb (marketplace tile description):
  Variant A: "Redwood sidecar adds low-latency LLM inference to your product. Deploy hosted or VPC-backed connectors with token-level observability, canary rollouts, and cost controls."
  Variant B: "Embed scalable LLM capabilities in minutes. Built for production: caching, autoscaling, and predictable throughput across regions."
- 3 benefit bullets (tile):
  • Predictable latency & autoscaling
  • Token-level cost visibility and quota controls
  • Security controls: KMS & audit logs

Trial / badge microcopy (for marketplace trial ribbon):
- "30-day trial — preconfigured sidecar; pay only for usage after trial"
- Short CTA: "Get started with sample connector"

Microcopy experiments (A/B examples):
- Option 1: Emphasize economics: "Cut inference costs with caching and batching—start free."
- Option 2: Emphasize reliability: "SLA-backed throughput and fast failover for mission-critical flows."
- Option 3: Emphasize developer speed: "Sample connectors + SDKs — deploy in under an hour."

Assets to collect from partner (pre-publish):
- 350x250 hero image (PNG, transparent bg OK)
- 640x360 screenshot set (3) showing partner UI with Redwood features highlighted
- Partner logo SVG + alt text
- Short customer quote (if available) or brief use-case paragraph (<= 200 words)
- Dedicated contact for post-launch ops

Marketplace publishing checklist (ops-focused):
- SKU mapping confirmed (billing owner)
- Trial entitlement config tested (billing sandbox)
- Legal T&Cs and data residency flags OK
- Listing privacy statement includes: "We may route inference to Redwood Inference; data retention limited to token-level telemetry for 30 days unless customer requests otherwise."
- Acceptance test script in place (see QA below)

Lightweight technical gating (preflight)
- Network / connectivity
  • Clear plan for sidecar networking: connector pattern, egress IPs, VPC peering or private endpoints
  • Firewall / CIDR allowance doc created for partner infra
- Authentication & keys
  • KMS integration plan confirmed for customer-managed keys (if requested)
  • Token lifecycle & rotation plan documented
- Runtime requirements
  • Minimum memory/CPU or GPU profile callouts for high-throughput routes
  • Expected seq length and throughput baseline from partner (sample traffic)
- Observability & telemetry
  • Tracing hook points (span names) and sample logs defined
  • Event mapping: request_id, model_name, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out
- Safety & content controls (if partner surfaces LLM output)
  • Safety model variant chosen for sidecar flows
  • Moderation hooks and fallback policy (reject/transform/route to human)

QA smoke tests (must pass to publish):
- Basic connectivity test: sidecar registers with control plane and responds to health check (pass/fail).
- Latency bench: p95 < agreed SLO for sample payload (pass/fail).
- Failure mode: simulate model OOM and verify automatic fallback to smaller variant (pass/fail).
- Billing telemetry: usage events appear in test billing stream (pass/fail).
- Security: sample KMS-encrypted secret rotates and remains readable by sidecar (pass/fail).

Launch contingencies / rollback playbook (quick notes)
- Soft launch window (recommended): 72 hours of monitoring, limited to 5–10 pilot customers.
- If latency regressions > 2x baseline or error budget >5% in 1h => auto-rollback to previous model variant + notify partner and operations.
- If billing spike > 3x expected in 24h => pause trial provisioning, throttle new requests, and investigate.

Telemetry dashboard knobs to create pre-launch
- Tile: Sidecar / partner-name – total requests, p95 latency, avg tokens per req, error rate, active connections
- Alerts: p95 latency > X ms for 10m, error rate > Y% for 5m, unexpected region routing >0
- Cost dashboard: cost per 1k tokens by model variant, caching hit rate, effective qps

Acceptance criteria for "green" publish status (short):
- All preflight checks marked done and owners signed off
- QA script: 5/5 pass items in staging environment
- Marketplace billing/test purchases validated in sandbox
- Partner marketing assets uploaded and alt text validated

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide canonical wording for privacy line in listing: data retention and PII handling. (Owner: Legal)
- Confirm whether partner will require a managed Dedicated pool (likely for high-volume sidecars) or rely on hosted fallback. (Owner: Sophie)
- Identify pilot customers and define traffic caps for soft launch. (Owner: Marco)

Notes to self / conversation history snippets:
- "Slack thread 2024-08-14: partner asks if we can surface token cost per feature. Feels high value for SMB buyers."
- "Linear RW-1024 is tracking connector onboarding work — includes infra tasks and billing mapping."

Next steps (immediate, in priority):
1) Send this doc to partner for copy review (Aisha)
2) Engineering kickoff to validate network diagram and sample payloads (Sophie)
3) Billing sandbox run-through next week (Ishaan)
4) Legal privacy blurb by end of week (Legal)

Version log:
- 2024-08-07 initial sketch
- 2024-08-21 added telemetry fields and microcopy experiments
- 2024-11-21 updated acceptance criteria and contingency thresholds after infra review

End of doc.
